title: Samsung is working on a central hub to track all your blocked calls
summary: This could likely be a One UI 9.5 special.
body: TL;DR Samsung is working on a dedicated Blocked calls dashboard for its Phone app in One UI 9.5. The dashboard shows calls blocked over the past 30 days, categorized into potential fraud, suspected spam, and manually blocked calls. The feature was manually enabled and is still in development, with no confirmed release date. Your Samsung Galaxy can already block unwanted calls , and the South Korean tech giant now appears to be preparing an easy way for you to keep track of just how many such calls your phone has filtered out. For what it’s worth, blocked-call history isn’t entirely new. You can already head to the Phone app > Recents > the three-dot menu and toggle on/off the option to view/hide blocked calls. However, what Samsung seems to be working on is a more detailed dashboard.

But Microsoft isn’t the only company trying to bring PCs and phones closer together. OnePlus is rolling out a new feature that would be very convenient for PC users. title: Google’s November update is breaking Pixel cameras, but there’s an easy fix
summary: Cameras are going dark, literally.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series owners report that their cameras stopped working after installing Google’s November update. Affected users are encountering black camera previews, error messages, and nonfunctional front and rear cameras. Completely powering off the device for around five minutes appears to resolve the issue for some users. Google’s big November update appears to have introduced a frustrating bug that leaves Pixel owners with completely nonfunctional cameras. That’s certainly a big concern, considering that cameras are one of our phones’ biggest appeals. Thankfully, it’s easy to fix the issue. Although this isn’t a universal issue, it clearly isn’t an isolated one either. Similar to the wireless charging bug we reported earlier, users have taken to Reddit and the Google Support forum to air their frustration. Reports suggest that the issue is only prevalent on Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series devices, with no reports from anyone with an older phone.

title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid mounting scandals
summary: CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.
body: TL;DR Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of NVIDIA. The move follows two scandals: an affair with a foreign intelligence agent and one with a direct NVIDIA report. CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO as the board searches for a replacement. In a move that has seemed inevitable for the past few days, Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of NVIDIA, according to a statement from the company . The decision was announced by NVIDIA’s board of directors who appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Kress will serve in both roles until NVIDIA appoints a permanent replacement CEO. The board said it is considering both internal and external candidates.

title: Tested: This unofficial AMD driver let me play Tears of the Kingdom on an Exynos phone
summary: Our own testing sees mixed results in other games, but there's great news if you're a Zelda fan.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A new open-source Vulkan driver for Galaxy devices with Exynos chips has surfaced online. Users online have reported significant improvements when playing PC games and Switch titles on their Galaxy devices. We’ve seen mixed results in our own testing, although Tears of the Kingdom saw huge gains. Snapdragon-powered devices are often considered the best for emulation , and that’s largely due to the rise of open-source Turnip drivers. These unofficial GPU drivers can deliver significantly better performance and compatibility in many emulators. Samsung phones and tablets with Exynos chips have mostly been left in the lurch as a result, resulting in inferior emulation. However, a new custom driver has delivered a major boost. Developer JimVulkan released radv-xclipse on GitHub last month for Samsung phones with Exynos chips. This is a port of the open-source RADV Vulkan driver for AMD GPUs. Of course, it’s worth noting that recent Exynos processors have Xclipse GPUs based on AMD graphics technology.

title: Scotland’s Flow Country
summary: Blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands store vast amounts of carbon.
body: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Scotland’s Flow Country Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search March 4, 2024 Compared to ecosystems in many other parts of the world, the blanket bogs of the Flow Country in northern Scotland are unassuming—soggy, treeless landscapes dominated by hummocky mosses, grasses, and heathers. Yet, to ecologists, the seemingly desolate areas are nothing short of extraordinary. The bogs store tremendous quantities of carbon . That’s because their soils are so waterlogged that microbes cannot fully break down dead plant material, a process that would otherwise release carbon dioxide. Instead, partially decayed plant matter accumulates into thick layers of spongy, crumbly, carbon-rich material called peat .
